feature_facts: DeadLetterNamingConvention formats a RoutingKey with a caller template and the default .dlq suffix.
InvalidMessageNamingConvention emits the .invalid suffix for invalid-message routes.
MessageRejectionReason preserves the RejectionReason enum value and nullable Description.
IAmAMessageScheduler is passed unchanged through CombinedChannelFactory and its nested factory.
MqttSubscription preserves independent dead-letter and invalid routing keys.
DontAckAction preserves its Message and InnerException while the sync and async attributes resolve open generic handlers.
DeferMessageAction exposes a nullable Delay and treats zero milliseconds as the subscription default.
ConfigurationException is raised synchronously when InMemoryMessageProducer has no scheduler for a positive delay.
ReceiptHandleIsInvalid is absorbed after an expired SQS receipt while the visibility change is attempted.
AccessDenied remains observable from the SQS acknowledgement path instead of being swallowed.
TopicPartitionOffset metadata drives Kafka Nack seeks and missing or wrongly typed metadata is a no-op.
ReadOnlyMemory<byte> backs MessageBody.Memory without an eager copy and Value is cached by content.
IAsyncDisposable governs repeatable asynchronous RabbitMQ producer disposal before send operations.
BasicAcksAsync and BasicNacksAsync confirmation callbacks detach exactly once during RMQ cleanup.
ChannelAsync.DisposeAsync awaits the consumer disposal and invokes it once across repeated calls.
TaskScheduler.Default owns the message pump task returned by Performer.Run.
ObjectDisposedException wins over cancellation for post-disposal RabbitMQ SendAsync and context Send.
SpyCommandProcessor records the exact request and clears RecordedCalls, Commands, and DepositedRequests on Reset.
PipelineValidationResult keeps errors separate from warnings and warnings alone remain valid.
PipelineValidationException carries the same PipelineValidationResult that made IsValid false.
ValidationProviderRegistrations preserves independent Sync and Async provider flags.
RequestValidationError preserves PropertyName, ErrorMessage, AttemptedValue identity, and ErrorCode.
PublishConfirmationResult preserves Success, MessageId, Topic, and nullable PublishSpanContext.
InvokeAllAsync awaits confirmation callbacks sequentially and stops before later subscribers after an exception.
Message.ProducerTopicHeaderName remains a local lookup key while wire topic headers and ordinary values pass through.

voice.handoff_rule: A handoff names the evidence path, the owner who can answer it, and the condition that makes the answer actionable.
voice.closure_rule: Close work only after the implementation, the focused regression, and the cross-package lifecycle consequence agree.
evidence_artifacts: Raw logs and exit code for dotnet test on the same commit
Reproducible diff records for the baseline, candidate, and rollback
Comparison of minimal inputs and visible outputs for cross-package calls
announcement_topics: Native regression testing and release withdrawal
announcement_details: In announcements, include only the versions that have been run, scope of impact, owners, and the next update time
Keep technical root causes in the corresponding module threads; announcements should link back to the original evidence without copying customer data
During the freeze, confirm the rollback entry point first, then decide whether to expand the set of callers

Error classification for SQS ReceiptHandleIsInvalid and AccessDenied

behavior_shape_matrix.domain: C# messaging transport and command-processor lifecycle contracts

dimensions.review_question: Which caller-supplied value must remain distinguishable from an omitted or default value at this boundary?
What state transition is observable, and which repeated call must leave the transition idempotent?
Which object owns the resource or cache, and how does that ownership constrain cleanup and reuse?
Which failure is intentionally absorbed, and which neighboring failure must remain visible to the caller?
Which downstream integration consumes this shape, and what identity or ordering must cross that boundary unchanged?
What exact return container, completion timing, or identity guarantee can a caller observe without inspecting internals?
When two signals compete, which one wins dispatch and where is that precedence documented for the next owner?

disclosures.contract: ChannelAsync.DisposeAsync completes only after the underlying consumer disposal has completed, while InvokeAllAsync remains an independently ordered callback boundary and repeated calls do not invoke disposal again.

DeferMessageAction exposes a nullable Delay so a positive requested duration is distinguishable from the zero-duration subscription default, and PipelineValidationResult keeps that outcome separate from warnings.

TaskScheduler.Default is the dispatch boundary for the message pump even when the caller is running on an exclusive scheduler, and ConfigurationException identifies a missing scheduler before work is queued.
PublishConfirmationResult preserves the wire Topic and publish context while the local Message.ProducerTopicHeaderName lookup remains filtered from transport headers.
